subject: Embedded runtime bundling discussion — Aurora Analytics + Redwood
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Celine Park <celine@auroraanalytics.com>, Tom Rivers <trivers@cloudforge.io>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:21:00 -0800
Subject: Embedded runtime bundling proposal — Aurora + Redwood

Hi Celine / Tom,

Great to meet briefly at the conference last week — thanks for the follow-up. Aurora's product roadmap (the search + assist workflow you demo'd) lines up nicely with a bundled offering that embeds Redwood's inference runtime into partner platforms.

High-level proposal: we provide a white-label/runtime bundle that your engineering team bundles into Aurora Studio. Key pieces:
- Runtime SDK and integration docs (lang agnostic client + Docker runtime).
- OEM license (term sheet attached) with branding rules and a revenue-share option.
- Dedicated support SLA for the bundled runtime (initial onboarding + quarterly health checks).
- Optional private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for named enterprise customers.

Attached: RW-ISV-term-sheet-v1.pdf (term sheet stub).

Questions for you:
1) Would Aurora prefer a per-customer seat-based license, an annual committed compute minimum, or a revenue-share-first model for initial pilots?
2) Do you require SOC 2 / compliance extracts before legal can move? We can share a redacted summary.
3) Who on your side should we loop for an engineering sync (API + auth)?

If the scope above matches your expectations, I can loop in Partnerships and Solutions Engineering to draft a mutual action plan.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachment: RW-ISV-term-sheet-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 32KB)
From: Celine Park <celine@auroraanalytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivers <trivers@cloudforge.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embedded runtime bundling proposal — Aurora + Redwood

Diego — thanks, excited to explore this.

Quick responses:
- Pricing: for pilots we prefer minimal upfront — a small annual commit plus revenue share on premium features. For enterprise customers we'll need an on-prem option.
- Compliance: yes, SOC 2 snippets and a short security questionnaire are standard for our procurement. Can you share a summary and any pen-tests you have?
- Engineering contact: Tom Rivers (cc'd) will lead integration from our side; he may want to engage earlier than procurement.

Can you also send a short mutual action plan with proposed milestones? A 6–8 week pilot timeline is typical for us. Attached is our product deck so you can see where we'd embed the runtime.

Thanks — Celine
Celine Park
VP, Product Partnerships — Aurora Analytics

Diego / Marissa — quick plan from Partnerships:

Pilot SOW (6 weeks):

- Week 4: Pilot evaluation with 2 customer use-cases; latency/cost dashboard visible to Aurora.
- Week 5–6: Wrap + success review + roll-to-prod checklist.

Pricing options (initial):
- Pilot: $10k annual commit + 10% revenue share on premium features.
- Enterprise: committed GPU-hour pool (tiered) + per-customer runtime license.
- Add-on: private deployment surcharge and premium 24x7 support.

Security package to assemble: SOC2 summary, redacted pen-test highlights, data retention and KMS notes. Marissa — can you draft the security attachment and a short SSO/auth checklist?

From: Tom Rivers <trivers@cloudforge.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Celine Park <celine@auroraanalytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embedded runtime bundling proposal — technical questions

Diego / Celine — thanks. A few technical clarifications from CloudForge (we run Aurora's integration):
1) Runtime footprint: Can Redwood provide a minimal Docker image and a slimmed quantized model variant for embedding into our hosted clusters? What sizes/benchmarks do you recommend for 8GB / 16GB GPU profiles?
2) Auth and licensing: Does the SDK allow runtime-level license keys per-customer and token-based telemetry to support revenue-share metering?
3) Offline/on-prem: For enterprise customers who require air-gapped installs, do you provide a patchable installer and documented security hardening steps?

If you can point to a short integration guide or example repo, that would accelerate our prep.

Tom Rivers
Sr. Integration Architect — CloudForge (partnering with Aurora)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>

Celine / Tom — thanks for the quick responses and the technical questions, and thanks Vanessa/Marissa for the internal sync.

Next steps I propose:
1) Engineering sync: Tue 2026-11-17 10:00 PT — deep dive with Tom, Marissa (SE), and our runtime lead to walk the SDK and deployment options.
2) Deliverables by Fri 2026-11-19: RW-ISV-term-sheet-v2.pdf (pricing & pilot SOW), SOC2-summary.pdf (redacted), and an integration checklist.
3) Pilot kickoff target: week of 2026-11-29, subject to access + NDA.

Answers to Tom's questions (brief):
- Image & benchmarks: we can provide a slim Docker image + quantized model variants. For 8GB profiles expect ~X tokens/sec and ~Y ms/seq (we'll attach a short benchmark table in the deck).
- Auth/licensing: SDK supports per-customer license keys and tokenized metering endpoints; we can export usage reports for revenue-share reconciliation.
- Offline/on-prem: we provide an installer bundle and a hardened checklist; on-prem installs require a comms-based license activation or offline license file.

Attachments: RW-ISV-term-sheet-v2.pdf (updated pricing & SOW), SOC2-summary.pdf (redacted compliance extract).

Please confirm the engineering sync slot or suggest another time. If you're aligned, I'll send calendar invites and route the v2 term sheet to legal for an expedited review.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
